title: r4 batch-shape exclusion silently neutralized the stale-bounce pins — the send_is_post_correction gate is no longer exercised by any test
evidence:
SET attempts = jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('at', to_char(now() - interval '1 hour', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'), 'channel', 'email', 'outcome', 'delivered', 'detail', 'old_send_1')),
           status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status
       WHERE id = $1::uuid
detail: stale_pre_correction_failure_stands_down_test (r3 W3) and same_day_stale_bounce_stands_down_test (r2 W1, the format-mix pin) both fixture a SINGLE email entry. The r4 batch-shape exclusion (email with no sms sibling at the same at) masks it in the find's EXISTS leg, and the contact fallback is cycles=0-only, so the corrected row is never found and the genuine_failure / send_is_post_correction gate never runs. Deleting the gate leaves both tests green — the typed TIMESTAMPTZ compare is now unpinned (the genuine control appends an sms sibling, so it only pins the exhaustion direction).
recommended_fix: Append an sms sibling at the same `at` to both stale fixtures (realistic two-channel shape) so the EXISTS leg matches and the stand-down is forced through the send_is_post_correction gate, restoring the r2/r3 pin.
